states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control, aiming for Wednesday morning, pending lab results and full medication history reconciliation before the cardiologist finalizes the plan. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit, and Nina can be updated on arrival windows if Marcus keeps the logistics-only setting active. states.content: Nurse Jamison is reviewing Marcus Reed's medications exactly as he is taking them right now, to prepare an accurate current medication list for review. As part of this review, Nurse Jamison asked Marcus whether he has taken anything over the counter for pain or colds; Marcus reported taking ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before he remembered he probably should not with the blood thinner (apixaban). Nurse Jamison says they will likely tell Marcus to stop ibuprofen because it raises bleeding risk with apixaban, and ibuprofen use should be flagged for medication review. Nurse Jamison also asked Marcus whether he has missed any doses of apixaban in the last month and whether there were any completely missed doses in the last three weeks; Marcus reported he has not missed any morning doses, reports no completely missed doses in the last three weeks as far as he remembers, and although he might have been a few hours late last Monday night when changing locations, he still took that pill before bed. Marcus also recalls that before cardioversion they were strict about not missing apixaban doses. Nurse Jamison will document the Monday-night apixaban dose as possibly delayed but not skipped. Nurse Jamison further asked Marcus about alcohol, supplements, or stimulants that could affect rhythm; Marcus answered that he does not drink energy drinks. Flag for medication review.

states.content: Over the past week Marcus Reed has had chest fluttering most evenings, shortness of breath climbing stairs, and one episode of lightheadedness on Saturday; he did not pass out. He also reports no chest pain and no bleeding, but has a racing heartbeat and feels washed out. His presentation is characterized as symptomatic atrial fibrillation/flutter with exertional dyspnea and lightheadedness, and no active bleeding. Clinician Dr. Patel confirms he is still in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response but is stable enough for an outpatient rhythm-control plan. He had shoulder pain last week, for which he took ibuprofen a couple of times before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner.
